subject: Day 38: board-book rotation refresh
bodyText:
Today's focus
Reading aloud is one of the highest-effect-size early-language interventions, and at this age repetition does the work. Today is about locking in a small fixed book set rather than chasing variety.

Action items
- Set a fixed rotation of three to five board books and read them daily; repetition, not novelty, is the vehicle for predictive language processing at this age. High-contrast and rhythmic-text titles work best now. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Order or borrow any missing staples for the rotation; a library card is free from birth and lets favorites repeat without buying every title. Reach Out and Read: https://reachoutandread.org/
- Confirm Avi's 2-month well visit is booked in the day 56-70 window; the visit anchors the first vaccine round and should not slip past day 70. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Frequent hiccups after feeds and occasional wet sneezing; neither needs intervention.
- [monitor] No social smile by 8 weeks. Most infants reach it earlier; if it is missing by then, raise it at the 2-month visit.
- [monitor] A persistent head tilt to one side with limited rotation may be positional torticollis; mention it at the next visit for a possible PT referral.
- [call within 24h] Poor feeding plus lethargy plus a clear drop in wet-diaper output as a cluster.
- [call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, blue color around the lips, or seizure-like activity: call the pediatrician same-day, and call 911 for blue lips or labored breathing!

Enrichment opportunities
- Keep the same three to five board books in daily rotation and re-read them often; predictable repetition is what drives early predictive language processing, so resist the urge to constantly swap titles. Reach Out and Read: https://reachoutandread.org/
- Smile and make eye contact to get Avi's attention, then wait for him to smile back. The social smile is consolidating this week, and these face-to-face exchanges reinforce it. AAP Bright Futures: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Prop Avi on a rolled towel under his chest for tummy time so his arms clear the floor; the slight incline lowers the effort of each head lift and keeps prone minutes accruing toward 30 a day. AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 41 (this week): Anoushka's 6-week postpartum OB visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit with the first vaccine round (HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1).
- Day 57-72: expect 24-48h of post-vaccine fussiness, low-grade fever, and drowsiness.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit with the second vaccine round.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
